A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Think-on-Graph 2.0 framework. All six pages of v1 and 22 pages of v4 are readable, including figures, tables, equations and v4's Appendices A–E. v1 contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark and component-ablation results for ToG2.0, including GPT-3.5 and Llama-2 experiments in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v4 reports original benchmark results, a newly constructed financial QA evaluation, sensitivity experiments, runtime measurements and manual analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The core pruning, retrieval and reasoning loop remains. However, v1 scores chunks against a query containing the question, clue query and triple; v4 Equation 5 instead attaches a verbalized triple to the scored context. v4 also introduces a self-consistency prepass setting (Section 4.3; Appendix B.4). These are limited procedural revisions within the retained framework.

E1.justification: v4 adds Creak, Zero-Shot RE and ToG-FinQA, expanding coverage to additional fact verification, slot filling and Chinese financial multi-hop QA. ToG-FinQA contains 97 questions. The earlier HotpotQA evaluation is now identified as AdvHotpotQA, a challenging subset; the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects a different underlying sample.

E2.justification: v4 adds explicit text-based Vanilla RAG and CoT-SC comparisons, evaluates GraphRAG on ToG-FinQA, and fills previously absent CoK comparisons on WebQSP and QALD-10-en. v1's Vanilla prompting corresponds to v4's Direct reasoning and is retained, rather than newly introduced.

E3.justification: FEVER changes from v1's blanket two-shot prompting to three-/six-shot demonstrations with an initial self-consistency step. Backbone experiments replace the reported Llama-2 configuration with Llama-3-8B, Qwen2-7B and GPT-4o. New experiments introduce retrieval-tool, context-count, width/depth and self-consistency-threshold comparisons, plus a manual analysis of 50 sampled outputs.

E4.justification: The original TP/RC/query-feedback ablation survives as Appendix B.2, Table 6. v4 substantially extends analysis with backbone comparisons, pruning-tool and context-count tests, width/depth sensitivity, self-consistency thresholds, measured runtime, evidence-source attribution, error categorization and additional QA cases (Sections 4.5–4.7; Appendices B and D).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v4's self-consistency experiments concern inference behavior, while its runtime averages and manual-category percentages are additional results rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive financial, backbone and diagnostic results and removes the Llama-2 result rows. Direct WebQSP changes from 74.55 to 65.9. Main FEVER results become 63.1/59.7 under revised prompting; the earlier 58.54 remains rounded to 58.5 in the appendix ablation. HotpotQA 40.91 versus AdvHotpotQA 42.9 is not an established same-setting gain. Proposed-method WebQSP/QALD scores only change rounding.

T1.justification: v4 Section 4.6 adds explicit LLM-call bounds: 2D+1 for combined pruning, WD+D+1 for separate pruning, and 2WD+D+1 for ToG. This extends v1's asymptotic pruning-cost argument. Most other added equations formalize existing search and weighted scoring; neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v4 expands the headline claims to SOTA performance on six of seven datasets, training-free portability across LLMs, applicability to associated graph/document collections, and smaller-model reasoning comparable to GPT-3.5. It explicitly positions bidirectional KG×Text coupling as the contribution. v1 emphasizes accurate, interpretable graph-guided reasoning demonstrated on four datasets.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations concerning knowledge exposure, backbone capability, single-hop versus multi-hop tasks, and the respective roles of triples and documents. Appendix B.1 introduces substantive limitations involving missing knowledge, retrieval failures, misunderstood questions and exact-match false negatives. However, the new context-length explanation contradicts Figure 3b: LLM scores increase while reranker scores decrease overall.

D1.justification: v4 supplies pseudocode, full pruning/reasoning prompts, the Azure entity-linking implementation, explicit W=D=3 and K=10 settings, and financial-dataset construction procedures and statistics. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing that newly disclosed defaults changed. v1's GPU configuration and 256-token generation-limit disclosures are dropped.

R1.justification: Related work is reorganized around text-based, KG-based and hybrid RAG. Added discussion of GraphRAG and HybridRAG supports a substantive positioning change toward mutually improving graph and text retrieval through tight coupling. Additional references cover Self-RAG, self-consistency, context filtering and the expanded datasets.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method exposition are extensively rewritten and reorganized. v4 standardizes the ToG-2 name, changes the title, separates graph search, context retrieval and reasoning explanations, adds a conclusion and thematic appendices, and relocates the original component ablation.

P2.justification: The ACM two-column presentation becomes a single-column preprint. Both principal diagrams are redrawn, including a new loose-coupling hybrid panel in Figure 1. Performance tables are expanded and regrouped, the retained ablation moves to the appendix, and new sensitivity plots, runtime/error tables, case diagrams and prompt tables substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important evidential gaps in v1 through explicit text-RAG and hybrid comparisons, financial-domain evaluation, controlled design studies, measured runtime and manual error analysis. Pseudocode, prompts and dataset documentation also make the framework substantially easier to assess. Reporting problems remain, notably Figure 3b's contradictory interpretation and the abstract's Llama-2 claim after its supporting result rows were removed, but these do not outweigh the substantial gains in experimental support and transparency.
